requirements.text: Patients should be able to book, cancel, and reschedule appointments online to reduce phone congestion.
Patients should be able to request repeat prescriptions online to save time for both patients and reception staff.
Patients should have secure online access to test results, but only after a clinician has reviewed them.
The portal must be user-friendly, especially for elderly patients or those who are less tech-savvy.
The portal must integrate smoothly with existing practice management software while ensuring compliance with GDPR and maintaining patient data security.
Patients should have a calendar view of available appointment slots, with filtering options by appointment type (GP or nurse) and reason for the visit.
The booking process should allow patients to select a preferred date and time, with confirmation available with a single click, including details like the clinician's name and appointment location.
Patients should be able to cancel appointments online without needing to call, and rescheduling should be straightforward, allowing them to pick another time immediately.
The system should flag urgent appointments, highlighting same-day options when necessary.
Patients should receive a confirmation that their prescription request has been received, along with an estimated time frame for when the prescription will be ready.
A secure messaging feature should be available for patients to ask questions or express concerns about their prescriptions without needing to call in.
The system must have checks to ensure compliance, with alerts for clinicians to review requests before approval, and the ability for them to decline or modify requests as necessary.
Patients should receive notifications via email or SMS when their test results are ready to view.
Upon logging into the portal, patients should have a dedicated section to securely access their results, complete with explanations or context from the clinician.
A feature should be available for patients to view historical test results over time, allowing them to track changes in their health.
The system should flag abnormal results and alert both the patient and clinician to prioritize urgent matters appropriately.
The interface should have a simple and intuitive design, featuring large buttons and readable fonts.
Navigation should be logical, with prominent access to key features like booking appointments and requesting prescriptions directly from the home page.
A guided tutorial should be implemented for first-time users, walking them through key functionalities using simple language and visuals.
Accessibility features should include options for text resizing and high-contrast themes, as well as compatibility with voice commands or screen readers.
There should be a dedicated help section with FAQs and instructional videos that are easily findable for patient support.
A clear method for patients to reach customer service for assistance should be established.
A feedback mechanism should be included, allowing patients to easily provide input about their experience to facilitate continuous improvement.
The implementation will need to prioritize features that deliver the most value within a limited budget.
Ensuring that the new portal integrates seamlessly with current practice management software is crucial.
Potential challenges may arise from existing infrastructure compatibility or performance issues.
Ensuring compliance with GDPR and Irish data protection regulations adds complexity to the project.
Consideration must be given to the training required for staff to effectively use the new system.
A strategy will be needed to encourage patient adoption of the portal.
